properties.state: {"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-08. Nothing here is intent and nothing has been chosen. THE IDEA, his words: \"the allocation of functions to systems/services should be done as late as possible (agreeing that doing it at genesis is too early). I feel like doing it at the last possible moment before functional allocation to system/service is the right call.\" It is the answer he reached to a caution raised against the sibling idea (dec:idea-the-ility-chooses-the-allocation-graph), which proposed ASKING at genesis what quality attribute the system is for: the objection was that at genesis you frequently do not know yet, and premature commitment can cost as much as late discovery. His resolution keeps the question and moves WHEN it is asked — not at genesis, but at the moment allocation actually has to be committed. WHAT THIS WOULD MEAN CONCRETELY: the quality-attribute question rides the ALLOCATION event rather than the project's beginning, so a design accumulates requirements and capabilities freely and is asked what it is optimising for only when something is about to be bound to a component. THE HOOK MAY ALREADY EXIST, and this is the cheap part worth checking before anything is built: `unallocated_capability` is already a detected gap, so the graph can already see capabilities that exist and are bound to nothing. The transition from \"capabilities exist, none allocated\" to \"the first allocation is being made\" is observable from graph state alone, which is the same state-not-history discipline dec:loop-status-state-not-history already commits to. If that is the trigger, nothing new needs remembering. OPEN SUB-QUESTIONS, none answered here: (a) is the moment per-PROJECT or per-CAPABILITY — a mature design allocates new capabilities continuously, so \"the last responsible moment\" may recur rather than happen once, which would make this a repeating prompt rather than a milestone; (b) does deferring allocation conflict with reflow2's own trajectory model, where `allocation` currently reads 100% and sits ahead of the `seams` frontier at 0% — if allocation is supposed to be late, a design showing allocation complete and seams empty may be describing a real inversion rather than healthy progress; (c) what happens to a design that never reaches the moment, since a demonstrator may sit unallocated forever and be right (maturity_report already refuses to say where a design SHOULD be). COUNTER-ARGUMENT, recorded beside rather than against: the last-responsible-moment principle assumes the cost of deciding late is lower than the cost of deciding wrong, which holds when deferral is free — and here it may not be, because artifacts get written against an assumed structure long before anyone calls `allocate`. If real files already embody a de facto allocation, then \"deferring the decision\" defers only the RECORD of it, and the graph would be late to something the build already did. That is the same as-designed-versus-as-built gap that granularity_report exists to surface, and it argues the trigger should watch ARTIFACTS appearing rather than the `allocate` call.","name":"OPEN — is allocating functions to systems/services something to defer to the last responsible moment, and can reflow2 tell when that moment has come?","rationale":"Recorded under the brainstorm skill, separately from the ility idea, because the two are genuinely different questions — WHAT drives allocation and WHEN it happens — and can be answered independently; one node holding both could only ever be half-answered. Worth keeping because it converts a raised objection into a design position rather than losing it: the caution was \"at genesis you do not know yet\", and this answers it without abandoning the question. The `unallocated_capability` hook and the artifacts-versus-allocate-call counter-argument are the two things a later session would otherwise have to re-derive.","status":"proposed"}
